title: Sample Size, ANOVA New
howtouse:
To compute sample size: specify the group means and power
To compute power: specify sample size and the group means

TIP: Sample Size, Power, Standard Deviation, and Significance Level below each accept a comma-separated list of values (e.g. 0.8,0.9). When more than one field has multiple values, every combination is computed and returned as a table, so you do not need to re-run this dialog for each scenario. Number of Groups and Group Means stay fixed for the whole run.
n: Sample Size per Group (comma-separated for multiple values)
grpmeans: Group Means, specify as values separated by commas, e.g. 20, 25, 40
siglevel: Significance Level (0-1; comma-separated for multiple values)
legends: Show Legends and if so, position of Legends (default is right)

help.title: Sample Size, ANOVA
help.body:
This is an assessment of sample size for a balanced one-way ANOVA. It computes the sample size or power, when the user specifies the other.

Number of Groups: Specify the number of groups in the study

Sample Size per Group: Specify the number of subjects in each group. Comma-separated lists are accepted.

Group Means: Specify the means in each group that you want to be able to detect. At least one mean has to be different than the others. This defines a single effect-size scenario for the whole run.

Power: Specify the desired power of the study, i.e. the probability that the test will reject the null hypothesis if the alternative hypothesis was true. Comma-separated lists are accepted.

Standard Deviation: Specify the standard deviation of the outcome. This is assumed to be the same across the groups. Comma-separated lists are accepted.

Significance Level: Specify the desired significance level (i.e. type I error) of the test. Comma-separated lists are accepted.

Generate Power Curve Plot: When multiple values are supplied for more than one field, check this box to plot the results. Choose which computed quantity goes on the X-axis, and optionally one or more fields to group/color separate curves by.

Required R Packages: stats, ggplot2
